scenario: AITA for getting mad at my bf for always walking in front of me? | Everytime my boyfriend and I are walking somewhere, he tends to walk much faster than me. I’m actually a pretty fast walker myself when alone, but when going out with him, either I’m in heels half the time so it’s harder to walk super fast, or even in flats, sometimes I just want to walk alongside him and hold hands and have a conversation. It’s hard to hear him or I’m struggling to keep up. I’ve brought it up to him multiple times but he says he just has longer strides (he’s maybe 6” taller than me) and can’t help it. We just went on vacation and walking around a new city, it was the same thing and I finally blew up at him saying that I don’t feel like his girlfriend when he won’t ever walk beside me. AITA and he really can’t help it?

I’m actually a pretty fast walker myself when alone, but when going out with him, either I’m in heels half the time so it’s harder to walk super fast, or even in flats, sometimes I just want to walk alongside him and hold hands and have a conversation. It’s hard to hear him or I’m struggling to keep up. I’ve brought it up to him multiple times but he says he just has longer strides (he’s maybe 6” taller than me) and can’t help it. We just went on vacation and walking around a new city, it was the same thing and I finally blew up at him saying that I don’t feel like his girlfriend when he won’t ever walk beside me. AITA and he really can’t help it?

Answer: <0 or 1>

prediction.raw: This is a **1** (not AITA—it’s understandable and valid). ### **Why?** 1. **It’s Not About His Strides—It’s About Connection** - Walking side by side (or even slightly behind) is a natural way to bond, hold hands, and communicate. If he’s always ahead, it can feel like he’s emotionally or physically pulling away, even if that’s not his intention. - Your frustration isn’t about his height or stride length—it’s about feeling *seen, paired, and connected* in a relationship. That’s a reasonable expectation. 2. **He’s Not Consciously Ignoring You** - You said he *can’t help it*—meaning he’s not doing it to be rude or dismissive. But even if he’s unaware, the effect is the same: you feel like you’re trailing behind, which can make you feel less like a "team." - Many people don’t realize how much walking style affects intimacy. If he’s never been told this bothers you, he might not realize how much it impacts your emotional experience. 3. **Your Reaction Was Valid** - You didn’t just *tolerate* this for years—you finally called it out, and that takes courage. If he’s truly committed to the relationship, he should reflect on how his habits affect you. - His response ("I can’t help it") is dismissive of your feelings, even if unintentional. A better approach would be: *"I love walking with you, but I want to make sure we’re both comfortable. Can we try walking side by side more?"* 4. **This Isn’t Just About Walking—It’s About Respect** - Small things like walking style, eye contact, or even how someone carries themselves can signal whether they’re *present* with you. If he’s always ahead, it can feel like he’s not fully engaged. - A healthy relationship means adjusting to each other’s needs—even if it’s just slowing down a little to match your pace. ### **What Now?** - **Gently Reframe the Conversation** (if you want to move forward): *"I know you can’t help your stride, but I just feel closer to you when we’re side by side. Can we try walking a little slower or adjusting so we’re more aligned?"* - **Observe His Response:** - If he *actually* tries (even just sometimes), that’s a good sign. - If he brushes it off again, ask yourself: *Does he make other small adjustments for me?* (e.g., holding your hand, remembering your preferences). - **Consider the Bigger Picture:** - Is this just about walking, or does it reflect a pattern of him being more focused on his own pace (literally or metaphorically) in other areas? ### **Final Thought:** You’re not being unreasonable—you’re asking for basic emotional connection. If he can’t even acknowledge this small thing, it might be worth asking: *Does he truly value our partnership, or is this just habit?* Either way, your feelings are valid. Would you like help brainstorming how to bring this up in a way that feels less confrontational?
